chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said: 'I came to the Imam, and he had preceded me by one rak'ah in the Fajr prayer. When he finished the prayer with the salam, it occurred to me that I had completed [my prayer], so I continued remembering Allah, the Exalted and Mighty, until the sun rose. When the sun rose, I stood up and remembered that the Imam had preceded me by one rak'ah. He said: 'If you are still in your place, complete with one rak'ah; and if you have already departed, then you must repeat [the prayer].'

key_terms.سَبَقَنِي بِرَكْعَةٍ: preceded me by one rak'ah (missed one unit)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I join the Imam in prayer but am unsure how many rak'ahs I missed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a latecomer who joins the Imam in the Fajr prayer but is uncertain if they missed a rak'ah due to distraction or delay. The Imam distinguishes between remaining in the prayer posture, which requires only one compensatory rak'ah, and having already concluded and left, which necessitates a full repetition of the prayer. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the physical state of the worshipper at the moment of realization.
